page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is a cost-efficient compute-oriented instance powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz. The instance features 16 vCPUs spanning 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core and dedicated CPU allocation. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache per socket. The CPU instruction set includes AVX, AES-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA support, though AVX-512 extensions are omitted. The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage or attached GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the e2-highcpu-16 exhibits mixed performance traits across execution types. It achieves strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25 percentile. Multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU ratings at 12,431.07, and Geekbench multi-core scores align in the middle 50 percentile range. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression register lower scores in the bottom percentiles. Memory bandwidth across uncached 256MB blocks reaches 71.67 GB/sec for reads and 35.27 GB/sec for writes. Real-world application benchmarks demonstrate solid execution rates, such as 15.91 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.91 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The e2-highcpu-16 instance delivers high virtual core density relative to its memory allocation, making it a practical choice for compute-parallel tasks that do not demand large per-thread memory capacity. The primary hardware tradeoff is its 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU limit, which restricts execution of large in-memory databases or memory-heavy analytics pipelines. Without local storage bundled, stateful deployment requires persistent cloud disk volumes. Given its 16 vCPUs and balanced middle-tier execution scores, this server is suitable for multi-threaded build compilation, static web serving, Redis caching, and lightweight background batch processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is a compute-oriented instance engineered for cost-effective multi-threaded processing. Equipped with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical Intel Xeon x86_64 cores operating at 2.2 GHz, the instance provides dedicated CPU allocation alongside 16.0 GB of RAM. It lacks local SSD storage and dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core stress-ng performance alongside average multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics across Geekbench, PassMark, and Redis tests. Single-threaded text decompression and file compression perform in lower percentiles. With a lean 1.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio, the e2-highcpu-16 provides a resource-dense CPU layout for budget-sensitive parallel workloads. It is well suited for concurrent web serving, build compilation, caching layers, and lightweight containerized services that do not require high memory overhead or local ephemeral storage.
